original_test_intent: Verify the BMC OEM Firmware page completes an approved firmware update and, only after a genuine successful terminal result, clears both the previously selected target device and uploaded file controls so stale selections cannot be reused accidentally.
original_method: Select the unique row; identify BMC/SUT and OEM target component; obtain the signed compatible image and vendor recovery plan; establish maintenance, stable power/network and backup console; open the exact WebUI page and capture target/file fields before selection; select the approved device and image and record UI state; submit one update; preserve UI and backend task progression without refresh/interruption; capture the success popup and terminal task; verify active/staged firmware and device health; inspect the same form/session for both cleared controls and absence of residual file metadata; document final state.
manual_activity: An operator supplies and approves the target/image and maintenance/recovery plan and supervises the state-changing flash; browser automation may capture the exact pre/post form and task states after confirmation.
required_inputs: BMC/SUT and exact OEM component instance/model/serial/current firmware identity
Approved target firmware image, version, hash/signature, compatibility and upgrade/downgrade intent
BMC WebUI/firmware build plus exact success popup, backend task terminal state and form-reset UI expectations
Protected account, stable power/network, workload drain, activation/final-state and rollback/reflash/recovery procedure
safety_requirements: Bind the selected form device and image to immutable approved identities before submission
Use a dedicated/quiesced SUT with stable management and recovery access
Submit one update and do not refresh, close, navigate away, interrupt or start another job until terminal state
Verify active/staged version and target health independently of the popup and cleared controls
Stop on wrong target/image, validation error, lost session/access, timeout/partial task or hardware fault; never auto-retry
agent_execution_scope: Record pre-selection, selected and post-success WebUI control states without exposing secrets/local paths
Submit only the approved single update after explicit confirmation and observe its documented terminal task
Collect success popup, version, health and exact cleared target/file state
Do not choose an image/target, authorize flash/activation, interpret a reset form as firmware success, retry or decide verdict
engineer_actions: Approve WebUI build, exact backend task/success oracle and when form reset must occur
Approve activation, maintenance, final state, rollback/reflash and independent recovery
Review flash and UI evidence and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The browser workflow matches the source and correctly requires a user image, but it must distinguish real task success from a popup and independently test the target/file controls after completion.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the approved BMC WebUI session to capture initial/selected controls, submit exactly one verified image to one verified device, await the defined backend terminal success, then inspect both selectors in the same documented post-completion state and separately verify firmware health.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Operations > OEM Firmware WebUI, actual flash, success popup, device/file clearing and 5/20-minute estimate remain.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Correlate browser DOM/screenshots, network/task identifiers and FirmwareInventory across a one-shot approved update, with explicit assertions that both device and file values become empty only after terminal success.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds immutable target/image identity, backend task correlation, exact reset timing, independent version/health proof and recovery boundaries.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A success popup can be stale or premature, and a page reload can clear fields regardless of update outcome; neither alone demonstrates the required post-success form behavior.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Firmware updates may restart the target or BMC and invalidate the browser session; the project must define whether the form is evaluated before restart, after reconnect or after an explicit page reload.

project_override_considerations: If the product deliberately retains a target selector while clearing only the file for usability, that behavior conflicts with the current Criteria and requires an approved Review-layer decision; it must not be silently accepted. Browser automation must not reveal a local firmware path or credential in artifacts.
expected_evidence: BMC/SUT/OEM target component plus current/target firmware identity
Timestamped initial, selected and post-success device/file field DOM values and screenshots
Secret-redacted update request/task identifier, progress and terminal result plus success popup
Active/staged version and target/BMC/SUT health evidence
No-interruption/no-retry audit, final state, recovery events and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The Procedure and Criteria consistently require a real successful OEM firmware update followed by cleared device and file fields. Exact update and UI semantics are omitted project details, not contradictions.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The WebUI operation and reset assertion are clear. A verified target/image, success oracle and recovery path are normal firmware prerequisites, so the case remains conditionally executable.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Functionality row 2235 Wistron-BMC Sanity-00017-V001: approve the BMC/SUT/WebUI build and exact OEM component instance/model/serial/current version; target image/version/hash/signature/compatibility and intent; exact WebUI device/file control states, backend update task and success-popup oracle, reset timing relative to reconnect/reload, active/staged version and health check; maintenance, activation, final state, timeout, abort and rollback/reflash/recovery.

review_improvement: Preserves the source's actual flash-dependent UI reset test while separating firmware success, browser lifecycle and both cleared controls into traceable assertions with critical recovery gates.
independent_technical_reasoning: The feature under test is not generic firmware update functionality but the form's state transition after success. A browser reload, session reset or BMC restart can clear HTML fields independently of a successful flash, while a success popup may appear before activation. Evidence must therefore correlate one immutable target/image, one backend job and the precise DOM state at the approved completion boundary, then verify firmware health separately. Because reaching that boundary requires a real OEM flash, a harmless mock or UI-only test would lose the source's coverage and the operation requires explicit human approval.
